title: SLO simulator: routing & heatmap quick-play (sales draft)
content:
Purpose:
A compact sales-focused playbook that helps AE/SE run a quick SLO-simulation demo (latency vs cost vs quality) and show a routing/ fallback heatmap to customers. The goal is to convert abstract claims (we reduce per-token cost / keep latency SLOs) into a short, interactive persona-driven convo and an on-the-fly visual: the routing heatmap.

Status / audience:
- Draft: operational notes and demo script for SDR → AE handoff and for SE enablement.
- Primary users: platform-sellers, SEs, and field engineers running discovery or technical qualification calls.

One-sentence play:
Walk customer through a 10-minute SLO-simulation: pick two routes (fast-hosted vs cost-optimized ded.), run simulated traffic mix, show heatmap of request routing + cost delta, then propose one small pilot (canary 5% routes for 2 weeks).

Why this is useful to sales (pain points we address):
- Customers ask "How will this affect latency and bill?" — we can show a simulated distribution rather than a single number.
- Turns an engineering question into a visible artifact (heatmap) that product folks take back to their ops and procurement teams.
- Encourages buy-in for reserved capacity by making unit economics tangible.

Preparation checklist (2–5 minutes before call):
- Open SLO-sim notebook (link above) or SLO-sim web UI.
- Load sample workload: "Customer A - chat + embeddings mix" (pre-saved in repo).
- Pick models: rwdx-22b (latency tier) and rwdx-8b-q4 (cost tier).
- Quick script lines below saved as "demo-scenarios/field-quick.json" in repo.
- Have Canary pilot template (email + scope) in Google Drive quick templates folder.

Demo script (10 minutes):
1) 60s pitch: "Most customers trade between cost and latency — today we’ll show what that distribution looks like on your traffic profile and what a safe canary rollout would be."
2) 60s workload selection: show the workload mix (%chat vs %embeddings vs %search) — explain skew matters.
3) 90s run: start SLO-sim with 1,000 simulated requests over 5-minute window. Show: median P95 P99 latencies and per-token cost estimates for each route.
4) 90s heatmap: switch to routing heatmap view — x axis: time slices; y axis: routing decision (region/model/capacity tier); color: per-request latency or cost. Narration: point out clusters where cost spikes or latency violations occur.
5) 90s fallback scenario: enable fallback policy (auto-route to ded. fallback when latency > threshold OR KV-cache miss) and re-run. Highlight how fallback reduces P99 at cost of X% more token spend.
6) 60s ask: propose next steps (pilot, dedicated sizing, SLO review workshop).

Quick numbers cheat sheet (to memorize):
- Typical P95 improvement when enabling local ded. fallback: 20–40ms for chat workloads (depends on model size).
- Median per-token cost delta between rwdx-22b and rwdx-8b-q4: ~3–4x (varies by quantization).
- Example pilot ask: 5% traffic for 2 weeks → yields enough telemetry to estimate real P95 and monthlyized cost within ±10%.
(Include note: numbers are illustrative; always run sim with customer profile.)

Objection handling (fast patterns):
- "We can just run our own load tests": yes, but we provide routing-aware heatmaps and fallback sims in minutes and tie them to cost math — faster decisioning for procurement.
- "Reserved capacity is expensive": walk pilot → show per-token vs reserved amortization for typical throughput (use small calc below).
- "Latency isn't consistent": show heatmap (temporal view) to reveal bursty behavior and how prefix caching/batching reduces variance.

Short role-play scripts (for SE rehearsal):
- SE: "If we route 80% to cost-tier, 20% to latency-tier during peak, what happens to P99?"
- AE (running sim): "Run it for your profile — look at the dark band at t=03:30; that's where cache miss bursts cause fallbacks, P99 spikes from 420ms → 630ms; enabling canary fallback drops that to 450ms at +8% cost."

Pilot framing & email template (placeholder text):
Subject: Quick 5% canary to validate SLO & unit economics
Body: Hi <Name>, proposing a 2-week 5% traffic canary to measure real P95/P99 and monthlyized cost. We'll: 1) mirror X routes to Redwood, 2) enable routing policy: latency-first, fallback to cost tier, 3) share daily heatmap and final workshop.

Playbook metrics to capture during pilot:
- P50/P95/P99 latency per route
- Per-token cost by model + overhead (network, API)
- Cache hit ratio and KV cache amplification
- Fraction of requests that triggered fallback

Handy commands / clipboard snippets (for demos):
- sim run --profile customer-a --duration 300 --workload mixA --routes fast:0.2,cost:0.8
- heatmap export --format png --range last5m
- policy set --name "canary-latency-5pct" --routes fast:0.05,cost:0.95 --fallback-enabled true

Open questions / follow-ups (notes to self):
- Need a one-click shareable heatmap PNG export from the sim UI (ask infra: GTM-842).
- Add a sample spreadsheet calc that spells out reserved capacity amortization per 1M tokens.
- Create a short 60s Loom video of the demo for SDRs.

References & artifacts:
- link: SLO-sim web UI (internal) — add to deck for AE quick access.
- sample workloads: /repo/slo-sim/sample-workloads.md
- proposal templates: Drive > go-to-market > quick-templates > canary-email.md

Notes / rough thinking (raw):
- Might add a "churn band" visual that overlays customer SLA windows (e.g., business-critical vs background flows).
- Consider a version that focuses only on embeddings-heavy customers (different heatmap color scale).
- Keep script sub-60s per section so AE can run 10-minute deep-dive during discovery.

Action items (owner):
- Ethan: wire up quick export endpoint on sim UI (due 2026-02-22).
- Samira: draft canary legal header for field pilots (due 2026-02-18).
- Jonah: create Loom 60s capture and add to repo (due 2026-02-20).

End of doc — lightweight, field-ready draft. Feedback welcome; mark comments inline or drop into #g2m-slos on Slack.
